title: Finite etale restriction to a nonempty clopen source over an irreducible base
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $X$ irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $p:Y\to X$ be finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be a nonempty subset that is both open and closed, endowed with its open subscheme structure, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be its inclusion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $p\circ j:U\to X$ is finite etale and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. No normality, integrality or Noetherian hypothesis on either scheme is assumed.

source.place: Tags 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite), 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), and 03WT (lemma-etale-open): restriction to a clopen source subset, followed by the open-and-closed image argument over an irreducible target.

proof.text: The inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ is an immersion: it factors as the identity closed immersion $U\to U$ followed by the given open immersion, using the definition of immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its image is exactly the closed subset $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] to conclude that $j$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 01IQ (lemma-immersion-when-closed), applied to the inclusion of a clopen open subscheme.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], the closed immersion $j$ is finite. Since $p$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] gives that $q=p\circ j$ is finite. Since $j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is etale, clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] give that $j$ and then $q$ are etale.

Put $A=q(U)\subseteq X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], clause (1), to the finite morphism $q$ and the closed subset equal to its entire source; this shows that $A$ is closed. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] to the etale morphism $q$ and its entire source, which is open; this shows that $A$ is open. Choose $u\in U$ using the assumed nonemptiness; then $q(u)\in A$, so $A$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tags 01WN (lemma-finite-proper) and 03WT (lemma-etale-open): finite maps are closed and etale maps are open.

proof.text: Both $A$ and $X\setminus A$ are closed and $X=A\cup(X\setminus A)$. By the closed-cover definition of irreducibility [def-weil-irreducible-components], either $A=X$ or $X\setminus A=X$. The second alternative contradicts $q(u)\in A$ from step 3. Thus $q(U)=X$, which is exactly surjectivity by [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Along with steps 1 and 2 this proves every assertion.

source.place: Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components): a cover by two closed subsets is trivial.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of Tags 035C, 01WK, 02GP, 02GN, 01WN, 03WT with Schemes Tag 01IQ and the definition of irreducibility.
